newsitem.title: UK: London gold price hits selling, rally slows.
newsitem.headline: London gold price hits selling, rally slows.

text.p: Gold prices were running into selling around $381.50 per ounce on Tuesday morning leading some dealers to think the week's rally was topping out.
"That extra dollar to $382.00 is proving difficult and we could see it checking at $380 if it dips off," one dealer said.
Gold was fixed at $381.60 per ounce up from $380.50 on Monday to record its highest fixing since October 29.
Volumes were fairly modest in early European trade and the rally had not generated much new volume buying yet.
Gold began its run when the investment funds finally had to buy metal as they gave up their bet that gold prices would tumble when they realised gold's floor would hold at $376.

Dealers also cited the weaker dollar against the yen as a support. "There is the chance of consumption being encouraged in the Far East now, which might have helped change the funds' attitude," one analyst said.
A dealer added, "It would be unfair to say that all of the rally has been because the funds have been covering these short positions. There has been some fresh buying as well."
However gold's efforts to rise further overnight were capped by selling from South African and Australian producers anxious to take advantage of the lift from last week's $377-$379 range.
Technnical analysts who study charts of previous prices to determine future price movements said gold was slotted into a $378-$383 range.
It was limited short term by the October 29 high of $382.35 with a "double top" from October 22 and 23 providing a further barrier at $384.30.
"We will not see more on the upside today," an analyst said.
However, analysts and dealers felt more favourably towards silver's price potential in the short term.
"Silver looks pretty steady having established its support (at around $4.72). It seems to have moved into a $4.75-$4.95 range," one analyst said.

Dealers said the advantage silver had over gold was that its it would not be held back by producers selling into its rally. "Gold will be well supplied into anything on the upside but silver is moving into a bit of vacuum," one dealer said.
Platinum fixed at its highest level since September 25 at $388.25 (up $2.25) as it climbed to a premium over gold after recently hitting a slight discount.
But palladium was quiet and up just $0.25 at $117.25/$118.25.
